summary: This note describes the 2017 National Football League season, the 98th season in NFL history. The regular season's 256 games ran over 17 weeks from September 7 to December 31, 2017, with each of the 32 teams playing 16 games and one bye week. The season opened with the Kansas City Chiefs beating the defending champion New England Patriots 42-27 and is set to end with Super Bowl LII on February 4, 2018, at U.S. Bank Stadium in Minneapolis, Minnesota, between the NFC champion Philadelphia Eagles and the AFC champion New England Patriots.
one_line: Overview of the 2017 NFL season: schedule, opening game, playoff dates and Super Bowl LII matchup.
key_facts: The 2017 NFL regular season consisted of 256 games played over a 17-week schedule.
Each of the league's 32 teams played a 16-game schedule with one bye week per team.
The 2017 regular season began on September 7, 2017 and concluded on December 31, 2017.
The regular season concluded with a full slate of 16 games on Sunday, December 31, all of which were intra-division matchups, as it had been since 2010.
The 2017 NFL season is the 98th season in the history of the National Football League.
The Kansas City Chiefs defeated the defending Super Bowl LI champion New England Patriots 42-27 in the NFL Kickoff Game on September 7, 2017.
The 2017 playoffs were scheduled to start on January 6, 2018.
The Pro Bowl was scheduled for January 28, 2018 at Camping World Stadium in Orlando, Florida.
Super Bowl LII was scheduled for February 4, 2018 at U.S. Bank Stadium in Minneapolis, Minnesota.
The AFC champion was the New England Patriots and the NFC champion was the Philadelphia Eagles, who were to meet in Super Bowl LII.
The regular season included games on Monday nights, on Thursdays including the NFL Kickoff game in prime time, and on Thanksgiving Day.
